claims.text: Partial Co substitution in MnNiSi can lower the martensitic transition temperature.
Ge substitution for Si may also help lower the martensitic transition temperature.
Co, with or without Ge, can reinforce the bonding network and improve mechanical performance.
Stoichiometric MnNiSi has a martensitic transition temperature of approximately 1200 K.
Stoichiometric MnNiSi has poor mechanical performance, including brittleness.
A martensitic transition well above the magnetic-ordering temperatures prevents a useful coupled magnetostructural transition and produces low magnetization change.
Co is to substitute on Mn sites, while Ge is to substitute for Si.
The relevant MnNiSi-based crystal lattice can adopt Ni2In- and TiNiSi-type structures.
Changing foreign-atom content can alter covalent bond strengths and thereby influence the martensitic transition temperature in MnM'X compounds.
Co substitution decreases the martensitic transition temperature by modifying electron density and bond character.
Co substitution produces a microstructure with improved ductility or fracture toughness.
Placing the martensitic transition inside the Curie-temperature window enables a coupled magnetostructural transition.
A transition inside the Curie-temperature window maintains a large magnetization change and significant magnetocaloric effect.
The relevant Curie temperature for the proposed MnNiSi-based alloy is approximately 622 K.
Lowering the martensitic transition below 622 K is sufficient to place it in the Curie-temperature window.
The substituted alloy will have increased toughness and reduced brittleness relative to stoichiometric MnNiSi.
The substituted alloy will retain a robust magnetocaloric effect with a large magnetization change over a wide temperature range.
Excessive substitution may disrupt the magnetic sublattice or generate secondary phases, degrading both mechanical and magnetocaloric properties.
